subtitle: Tue Oct 27 → Mon Nov 2, 2026 · GT · HN · BZ · NI, El Salvador excluded · work 12:00–20:00 · sleep 23:00–07:00 · macro plan v1, 2026-09-04

inputs.anchor: Costa Rica by Mon Nov 2. Earliest/latest arrival not yet stated — assumed latest = Nov 2 evening, earliest = Nov 1 evening. If Nov 3 is acceptable, Nicaragua gains a full day for ~$60 (see quiet part). Mom in Panama Oct 23–27 is the fixed people-anchor before this leg.
inputs.work: 12:00–20:00 local (UTC−6). New York is +2h until the US clocks fall back on Nov 1, then +1h. No calls in transit. Coworking: Impact Hub Antigua; Caye Caulker and Granada are café/hotel wifi — book AC rooms with desks for call days.
inputs.sleep: 23:00–07:00 nominal. Plans A and B each carry ONE seat night (Linea Dorada luxury class, reclining, two drivers, ~8.5h) — the only overnight leg that exists in the region. Plan C carries none.
inputs.must-hit: Guatemala, Honduras, Belize, Nicaragua, then Costa Rica. Kite where it blows (late Oct is pre-season everywhere; Lake Nicaragua at Granada is the best odds). Lens: complexity economics.
inputs.luggage: Kite: harness + bar only, rent at Asese (Granada) and Atitlán; a full kite bag costs a fee on 4 flights and 3 of them are Cessnas with weight limits. Running shoes, swim kit. ≤3 luggage touches per day.
inputs.weather: Normals, not forecasts (pull the forecast the week before): Antigua 24/14 · Copán 28/17 · San Pedro Sula 31/22 · Caye Caulker 30/25 · Flores 31/22 · Granada 32/23 · San José 25/17. No city above 33°, so the 12–20 block holds. October is the wettest month; hurricane season to Nov 30 on the Caribbean side.
inputs.money: Cheap default computed first; upgrades priced as deltas. Advance fares vary 2x, so every number is a range.

hard_blocks: El Salvador excluded. Every Guatemala/Belize → Nicaragua flight connects airside in San Salvador (Avianca). If "excluded" includes airside transit, the only alternative is Copa via Panama City: +$150–250 and +3h per leg. Decide this before booking.

No overnight bus exists Managua → San José or Honduras → Nicaragua: the Peñas Blancas and Las Manos borders close at night (Peñas Blancas 06:00–22:00, Sundays 20:00). The region has exactly one overnight leg: Guatemala City ↔ Flores.
Nicaragua: online pre-registration form at solicitudes.migob.gob.ni, filed about a week ahead, plus a US$10–13 tourist card in cash at entry. Passport valid 6 months.

Belize land exit BZ$40 (US$20) cash at Benque Viejo; no fee entering Guatemala by land. CA-4 (GT, HN, NI, SV) is one 90-day zone; Belize is outside it, so re-entering Guatemala from Belize is a fresh stamp.
Hedman Alas San Pedro Sula → Copán runs only Sun / Thu / Fri at 11:00. Saturdays and Mondays fall to Casasola local buses (3–4h, US$6–10).

quiet_part: The night bus does not save money on this corridor. Plan B versus Plan C is about $90 apart and the seat night buys Tikal, not dollars. Flying every leg is the cheap-enough default here; overland purity would cost you Nicaragua.
Flying everything (Plan C) is $735–1,250 in fares for four legs. That is the trip. Choose it as one.
Nov 2 as a hard date is what starves Nicaragua. Sliding Costa Rica to Nov 3 buys a full Granada day (kite morning + intact work block) for one more bed, $40–80, and nothing else changes.
The El Salvador rule is silently touched twice (airside at SAL on the Managua flights). Routing via Panama instead is +$150–250 and +3h per leg. Say which you mean.
Tikal and a real Nicaragua do not both fit in six nights with the work block intact. Copán is the Maya-collapse stop in every plan; Tikal belongs to a later Belize + Flores trip in kite season.

hybrid.title: Plan C, plus four targeted moves
items: Book Tropic Air SAP → BZE first, for Fri Oct 30. It is the single point of failure in B and C. If Friday is not an operating day, shift the Copán block: shuttle Antigua → Copán Tue 27 afternoon is impossible (shuttles leave 03:30–05:00), so instead do Copán ruins Wed 28 after the 10:00 arrival, work 14–20, Hedman Alas 16:00 → SAP, and fly Thu 29 — Caye Caulker gains a day.
Granada: an AC room with a desk for Nov 1 (+$20–40 over the cheap bed). That block is the only full work day in Nicaragua; protect it.
Kite: rent at Asese both Granada mornings (US$50–80 a session, ~40% odds of the first Papagayo days). Skip the kite bag; it costs ~$100–150 in fees across four flights and two Cessna weight limits.
Nov 2: fly MGA → SJO in the afternoon ($120–250) rather than the 06:00 Tica Bus ($40). The $80–210 buys the last Granada kite window and six daylight hours.

If you want the seat night and Tikal anyway, take Plan B and verify two things before anything else: the Flores night-bus departure and the Belize City → Flores departure. Both are unverified and both decide whether Tikal is a sunset or a drive-by.

notes: Cash map: Guatemala Q (≈7.7/$), Honduras L (≈25/$), Belize BZ$ pegged 2:1 and USD taken everywhere, Nicaragua C$ (≈36/$) with USD widely taken, Costa Rica ₡. Pull local cash from bank ATMs on a debit card; decline DCC. Border fees are cash: BZ$40 out of Belize, US$10–13 into Nicaragua.

Stations, exact: Linea Dorada Guatemala City = 16 Calle 10-55, Zona 1 (taxi door to door at night). Belize City buses to Flores leave from the Marine Terminal on North Front Street, the same building as the Caye Caulker water taxi. Hedman Alas SAP = Boulevard del Sur, not the Gran Central. Tica Bus Managua = Barrio Martha Quezada.
Timezone: all five countries UTC−6, no DST. US clocks fall back Sun Nov 1 03:00: New York goes from +2h to +1h mid-trip; move the Nov 1–2 call slots accordingly.
Luggage: three Cessna legs (Tropic Air) and small shuttles. One carry-on plus a daypack keeps every day at ≤3 touches; the Copán shuttle and the night bus both take bags underneath.

Kite odds, honestly: Caye Caulker and Roatán are Dec–Apr spots; Lake Atitlán blows afternoons but is not on any of these routes; Lake Nicaragua at Granada opens in November. Two Granada mornings are the trip’s kite. Bahía Salinas, Costa Rica, opens the same week you arrive.

Recovery: Plan B’s seat night lands at 06:30 in Guatemala City with a flight at ~09:00 and a hotel at 15:00 — book the Granada room for early check-in and take the shower before the work block, not after.

Practice frameworks: pre-register the Tropic Air outcome (forecast: 70% Friday operates) before you look it up; pre-mortem the Nov 1 SAL connection (missed connection = Managua at midnight, Granada block dead); one micro-ask a day — the Copán guide about the 9th-century drought, the Asese instructor about when the Papagayo actually turned on last year.
